The laws that apply

The core rulebook is the Arkansas Residential Landlord-Tenant Act of 2007, Chapter 17 of Title 18 of the Arkansas Code. It governs private rental units. Government-subsidized housing is outside it.

The Act's stated aim is to simplify and modernize residential rental law. It covers what a rental agreement may contain, such as rent and the length of the term, and what each side must do when the other breaks the deal. Section 18-17-202 lists arrangements it does not reach: institutional residences for medical, educational or religious services, hotel and motel stays that are subject to sales tax, and protective shelters.

Tenants have duties too. Section 18-17-601 requires them to follow housing codes that affect health and safety, keep the unit clean and safe, dispose of waste reasonably and keep plumbing fixtures reasonably clean. Oral and written leases both bind the parties, though a written lease heads off arguments about who promised what.

Security deposits

A deposit is capped at two months' rent, but only for landlords who rent six or more dwellings. The rules in brief:

QuestionRule for covered landlords
Who is covered?Landlords who rent six or more dwellings, including a landlord who has someone manage the property or collect rent
Maximum depositTwo months' rent
Deadline to return it60 days after the tenant moves out
If money is keptA written, itemized list of charges within those 60 days
Keeping the whole depositAllowed when damage or unpaid rent exceeds it
If the landlord ignores the rulesThe tenant may be owed twice the deposit plus costs and attorney's fees

A landlord with five or fewer properties falls outside these provisions. In that case the written lease carries more weight, and a tenant can still sue in small claims court for the deposit, where the landlord may counterclaim for unpaid rent or damage. If a landlord makes a reasonable attempt and cannot find the former tenant, the whole deposit may be kept after 180 days.

Rent increases and ending a lease

Before raising rent, a landlord owes notice of at least one rental period, on oral and written leases alike. A landlord can also end a lease for any reason, giving one rental period's notice on an oral lease or whatever notice the written lease requires.

  • A tenant who wants to sublease usually needs the landlord's approval first, plus written direction on how much rent can be collected.
  • A tenant leaving a written lease follows its notice terms. A tenant leaving an oral lease gives one rental period's notice.
  • Under § 18-17-704, either side ends a week-to-week tenancy with seven days' written notice and a month-to-month tenancy with 30 days' written notice.

A landlord who declines to renew may do so for any reason except those the Fair Housing Act forbids.

Who handles repairs?

The answer turns on when the lease was signed. Under older arrangements, renters generally take a house or apartment as is, and the landlord owes no maintenance beyond what city building codes require. Any promised repair belongs in the lease. A tenant should keep paying rent even when a promised repair is missed. The realistic options are small claims court, renegotiating, moving out or hiring a private attorney.

A 2021 law changed things for newer leases. Under § 18-17-502, a lease signed or renewed after November 1, 2021 carries implied standards for a dwelling or single-family house: running hot and cold water, electricity, drinking water, a code-compliant sanitary sewer and plumbing, a working roof and building envelope, and heating and air conditioning if the home had them at signing.

The statute gives landlords some safe harbors. A landlord counts as compliant if the tenant receives a written defect form at move-in and either signs it without listing a defect or fails to return it within two business days. Damage caused by the tenant, family or visitors does not count against the landlord. A tenant may install a battery-powered or plug-in smoke or carbon monoxide detector at personal expense and then must keep it working. Stricter city or county housing standards still apply.

When a tenant breaks the lease

The first step is written notice. Section 18-17-701 allows a notice that names the acts or omissions and says the agreement ends at least 14 days after receipt unless the problem is fixed. Unpaid rent moves faster: once rent is five days past due, the landlord may terminate.

If a tenant refuses lawful access, a district court can order the tenant to allow it, because § 18-17-705 lets the landlord seek an injunction. A landlord can recover actual damages and, with a lawyer, attorney's fees if nonpayment was not in good faith. The steps from the three-day unlawful detainer notice through the sheriff's writ are covered on the Arkansas eviction process page.

Fair housing rules

The Fair Housing Act bars discrimination in renting or selling a dwelling based on race, color, religion, gender, handicap, familial status or national origin. Banned conduct includes:

  • Advertisements that signal a preference or limit, such as adults-only for part of a complex.
  • Different terms or conditions of sale or rent.
  • Discrimination in the use of facilities tied to the dwelling.
  • Assigning a person to a particular section of a complex or a particular floor.

Complaints go to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development or the Arkansas Fair Housing Commission.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Arkansas houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a rental house

A sale does not wipe out the duties above. Nothing in these statutes says a sale cancels a lease, so read the lease and get an attorney's advice first.

Owners weighing a sale usually look at three things. A month-to-month tenant can be given 30 days' written notice. A landlord who will not renew needs a lawful reason, and in Arkansas any non-discriminatory reason works. The deposit is separate: ask the closing attorney how it and any prepaid rent will be handled so the tenant's refund rights are protected.

A rental also changes the tax paperwork. Tell the assessor when a house goes from owner-occupied to rental. The transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration applies to the deed. In Little Rock, privately owned rentals with two or more dwellings must meet city minimum housing standards, which include working plumbing, electricity and a roof that does not leak.

A cash sale of a tenant-occupied house can close without repairs or showings, which helps when a tenant is hard to schedule. Gather the lease, the deposit amount, a rent ledger and any notices you have sent before you talk to a buyer.

Where to get help

Legal Aid of Arkansas runs a free helpline at 1-800-952-9243 for people who qualify, along with a landlord and tenant guide. The Arkansas Community Action Agencies are another resource. In Little Rock, housing code complaints go to the Department of Housing and Neighborhood Programs at (501) 371-6825, and 211 connects residents to utility and housing help.

Frequently asked questions

What is the maximum security deposit in Arkansas?

Two months' rent. The cap binds landlords who rent six or more dwellings, so a landlord with fewer properties is outside that statute, though the lease still controls.

How long does a landlord have to return a deposit in Arkansas?

Sixty days after the tenant moves out. A landlord who deducts must send a written, itemized list of charges within the same 60 days.

Can an Arkansas landlord raise the rent whenever they want?

No. The landlord owes notice of at least one rental period before a raise, on oral and written leases alike. Check the lease for any terms about rent during a fixed term.

Does a tenant have to keep paying rent if the landlord skips a repair?

Yes. Section 18-17-502 bars withholding or offsetting rent over implied quality standards. After written notice and 30 calendar days with rent current, the tenant's sole remedy is to end the lease without penalty and recover a deposit that is owed.

Can a landlord end a lease so the owner can sell?

A landlord may end a lease for any reason with the required notice, and a sale is not a special ground. Have a lawyer confirm the notice period for your lease before you send it.

title: Arkansas Eviction Notice Rules: Notice Types, Days and Selling the House
content:
Arkansas Eviction Notice Rules: Notice Types, Days and Selling the House

Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Arkansas Eviction Notice Rules sale
  • Turn the Arkansas Eviction Notice Rules offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Arkansas House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Arkansas?
We buy Arkansas houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Written notice before an eviction

Which notice you serve turns on why you want the tenant out. Unpaid rent usually calls for a three-day written notice to vacate. Separately, once rent sits unpaid five days beyond its due date, the law treats that as notice that the landlord may begin eviction.

A lease violation other than late payment runs on a longer clock. In that situation, Ark. Code 18-17-701 the landlord delivers a written notice that describes the acts or omissions and warns the agreement will end no sooner than 14 days after the tenant receives it. If the problem can be fixed and the tenant fixes it in that window, the lease continues.

An older criminal law covers rent defaults too. Under Ark. Code 18-16-101, willfully refusing to leave after ten days' written notice is a misdemeanor, with a fine of $1 to $25 for each day. Landlords rarely use it, though the ten-day figure still shows up on old forms.

SituationNotice or trigger
Rent unpaidThree days' written notice to vacate; five days past the due date gives the right to begin eviction (18-17-901(b))
Other lease breachWritten notice, termination no sooner than 14 days after receipt if not cured (18-17-701(a))
Week-to-week tenancyWritten notice at least 7 days before the end date (18-17-704(a))
Month-to-month tenancyWritten notice at least 30 days before the end date (18-17-704(b))
Rent default, criminal trackTen days' written notice, then a misdemeanor if the tenant willfully stays (18-16-101)

How the case moves after the notice period

Next the landlord goes to district court. Under Ark. Code 18-17-902, the filing is a complaint plus an affidavit of eviction signed by someone with personal knowledge of the grounds. After service, the tenant has ten calendar days to leave or explain to the court why not.

A tenant who receives the summons has five days to send a written objection to the court clerk. If none arrives, the county sheriff can remove the tenant. Since a sale date hinges on that deadline, ask the district court clerk handling your case to confirm it.

If the tenant contests, section 18-17-905 has the court hear it like any other civil case. Either side may appeal through the normal civil route under section 18-17-909. An appeal is what most often stretches a timeline past what an owner expected.

  • Step one: written notice that matches the reason for the eviction.
  • Step two: complaint and affidavit filed in district court.
  • Step three: order to vacate or show cause, served on the tenant.
  • Step four: hearing if the tenant contests, or sheriff removal if no one objects.
  • Step five: possible appeal by either party.

Ending a lease because you want to sell

In most month-to-month and oral arrangements, yes. A landlord may give notice of lease termination for any reason: one rental period's notice for an oral lease, or whatever the written lease provides.

Selling a rental? Start with the lease, because a fixed-term written lease still controls until it ends. For a month-to-month tenant, section 18-17-704 calls for at least 30 days of written notice, and some landlords choose a termination date that matches their target closing.

Document everything. If the tenant stays and the matter reaches a judge, your notice dates, delivery proof and lease copy become the evidence.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Arkansas house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

When the tenant stays past the lease

You can sue for possession. Holdovers fall under section 18-17-704(c): a tenant who remains without consent once the term ends or the agreement is terminated can be taken to court, and attorney's fees are available if the holdover isn't in good faith.

A willful holdover brings a stiffer remedy, which is the greater of three months of periodic rent or twice the actual damages, along with reasonable attorney's fees. Avoid accepting rent in a way that looks like consent to continued occupancy, since section 18-17-704(c)(4) points back to the rule for tenants who stay with the landlord's agreement.

When the court rules for the tenant, section 18-17-908 lets the tenant keep possession until the tenancy ends by agreement or law, until rent goes unpaid, or until another eviction succeeds. Any contract to sell with a tenant in the house should leave room for delay.

Belongings and the deposit

Items a tenant leaves behind once the lease ends count as abandoned. The landlord can handle them as seen fit with no recourse for the tenant, and a lien attaches to them for amounts the tenant agreed to pay.

The deposit statute reaches only larger landlords, meaning six or more dwellings. For them, the deposit can't exceed two months' rent, must be returned within 60 days of move-out, and any deduction needs an itemized written list inside the same 60 days. One or two rentals fall outside it, although your lease can still set terms.

  • Photograph the empty house and any left items before touching them.
  • Keep receipts for repairs charged against a deposit.
  • Send the itemized list to the forwarding address within the 60 days where the law applies.
  • Never push a tenant out by changing locks or cutting utilities. Go through the court.

Time and money costs

The filing fee comes from Ark. Code 16-17-705, cross-referenced in section 18-17-902, and the district court clerk can quote today's amount. Time is the bigger cost. Notice days, service, a hearing date and any appeal all add up, and each rental month lost in that stretch is income you don't get back.

Attorney's fees are recoverable in some cases. Section 18-17-701 allows them for willful noncompliance other than nonpayment, and for nonpayment not made in good faith, but only when the landlord is represented by an attorney.

Then come repairs after move-out. Rental houses that have been through an eviction often need paint, flooring or cleanout before they can be listed with a traditional agent.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Arkansas houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

A pending eviction and your sale

It narrows your options. A buyer with a lender usually wants possession, an inspection and a repaired house, none of which is easy while a tenant is contesting. Some owners wait out the court process and then list. Others sell with the tenant or the open case attached, to a buyer willing to take on that risk.

A cash buyer purchases as-is and doesn't depend on lender repair requirements, which can matter when a difficult tenancy left damage. Whether a sale makes sense before the eviction ends depends on the lease, the notice already served and the state of the court file. Talk to an Arkansas attorney or the district court clerk before you sign a contract.

Before you call a buyer, gather the lease, copies of every notice and its proof of delivery, the case number if one exists, and photos of the house. Those papers let a buyer and a title company judge the situation quickly.

Fair housing rules also apply to the sale and rental of homes. Advertising or terms showing a preference based on race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status or national origin are barred, whether the house is rented or sold.

Frequently asked questions

What is the notice period for nonpayment of rent in Arkansas?

Three days' written notice to vacate is the usual form. Ark. Code 18-17-901(b) also treats rent unpaid five days after the due date as legal notice that the landlord may begin eviction.

How long is the notice for a month-to-month tenant in Arkansas?

Written notice at least 30 days before the termination date under Ark. Code 18-17-704(b). A week-to-week tenancy needs at least seven days.

Can an Arkansas tenant be arrested for not leaving after notice?

Possibly. Ark. Code 18-16-101 makes it a misdemeanor to willfully refuse to leave after ten days' written notice for failure to pay rent, with a fine of $1 to $25 per day. Landlords more often use the civil eviction route.

Who removes a tenant after an eviction order in Arkansas?

The county sheriff. A tenant who doesn't file a written objection can be removed by the sheriff, and the summons in a rent case goes to the sheriff of the county where the complaint is filed.

Does an Arkansas landlord need a lawyer to evict?

No. The landlord or the landlord's agent can file the complaint and affidavit. A lawyer is needed only to collect attorney's fees under section 18-17-701.

Arkansas Tax Deed and Tax Lien Sales: Process, Redemption and Selling First

Selling a Arkansas House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Arkansas?
We buy Arkansas houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Tax liens or tax deeds in Arkansas?

Arkansas sells the land itself, through a state officer, and bars sales by the county. Ark. Code 26-37-101 says tax-delinquent land cannot be sold at the county level.

The county collector holds the delinquency for a year. If the owner has not redeemed by the certification date, the collector sends the parcel to the Commissioner of State Lands, who either collects the taxes or sells the property at public auction. A buyer at that sale gets a deed from the state, not an interest-earning certificate, so this page follows the deed path.

Timeline from missed payment to state auction

Over two years can pass between the missed due date and a sale. The state receives the parcel about a year after the due date, and a sale cannot come earlier than one year after that. The steps come from 26-37-101 and the Commissioner's rules.

TimingWhat happens
October 15Taxes become delinquent
One year laterCounty collector holds, then certifies the land after notice
By July 1 of the next yearLatest certification date
On receipt of certificationTitle vests in the State of Arkansas, in care of the Commissioner
At least 30 days before saleCertified mail notice of the sale and the right to redeem
At least 60 days before sale (homestead)Personal service if there is no proof of receiving the mail
At least 1 year after certificationEarliest sale date

Certification lists all taxes, penalties, interest and costs, along with the owner of record and last known address. The Commissioner takes no physical possession and owes no duty to maintain the property, so upkeep of the house stays with whoever occupies it.

Who must be notified before the sale?

The owner and interested parties of record get certified mail first. Section 26-37-301 sets the notice rules, and the Commissioner's rules add newspaper publication.

  • If certified mail comes back unclaimed or refused, the Commissioner resends by regular mail.
  • If delivery fails for another reason, a second notice goes to any other address in county property records, such as the one on the deed or a forwarding address held by the collector or assessor.
  • For joint tenants every owner counts, and for tenants by the entirety either spouse counts.
  • A homestead owner who cannot be shown to have received the mail is served in person at least 60 days before the sale, and that owner pays the extra cost.

The notice carries a short legal description, the parcel number, the sale date and a warning that the land will be sold unless redeemed. It goes to the owner of record at the last known address, so an heir who never updated the records may never see it. Only a person who did not receive notice in substantial compliance can challenge it.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Arkansas house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to redeem delinquent land

Pay the taxes, penalties, interest and costs, with a petition, before 4:00 p.m. Central on the last business day before the sale. The Commissioner's real estate division takes payment online through its Pay Taxes button, or by check or money order with a signed petition to redeem.

  • Have the parcel number from your tax bill.
  • Partial or incorrect payments are rejected and do not extend the deadline.
  • A quoted payoff stays valid for 30 days.
  • Anyone may redeem, and redeeming does not change who owns the property.

Call the division at 501-324-9422 or visit 7003 Valley Ranch Drive in Little Rock. A redemption deed is issued when the payoff is made, and a receipt goes to any redeemer who is not the record owner.

How the auctions work

Parcels go first to a public in-person auction. Any that fail to sell move to an online auction about 30 days later. The Commissioner's rules set the bidding terms.

  • Bidders register, get a bid card and show photo identification.
  • The highest bid at or above the minimum wins, and an accepted oral bid is binding.
  • Payment is due at the sale by check, certified funds or card. Cash and installment plans are refused.
  • Online, the winner pays $100 earnest money, or the whole bid if it is under $100, and the balance in certified funds within 10 business days.
  • State staff, the county collector or deputy, foreign-address entities, and former owners or interested parties cannot bid.

The bar on former owners matters if you are the seller. Once a house reaches auction you cannot buy it back at the sale, and redemption beforehand is the only way to keep it.

What the winning bidder receives

The buyer gets a limited warranty deed that conveys only the State's interest, and a court action to quiet title is often needed. The deed is issued after full payment and recorded with the county.

A 90-day litigation period also applies. A buyer at the state's sale therefore receives less than an ordinary seller would convey. For parcels unsold at the first auction, the online reserve bid equals the taxes and costs for the first two years, a figure tied to the debt and not to the value of the house.

Money bid above taxes, fees, penalties, interest and costs is excess proceeds. The Commissioner's costs and the county's taxes are paid first, then other government claims, and the remainder goes to the former owner less up to $500 for administration. Claims are denied unless every requirement is met strictly. Call the Commissioner's office for the current claim period before you count on a timeline.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Arkansas houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Notices before certification

Collectors publish lists before the state ever sees the parcel. In Craighead County the collector prepares a list of delinquent personal property taxes before December 1 each year for a legal newspaper, which must publish it within seven days. Delinquent real estate taxes are listed in a local newspaper after the deadline.

The Commissioner's division also keeps the county certification books and researches the title of each certified parcel before it notifies owners and interested parties. Each of those is a point where an owner can still catch the problem and pay the county or the state. A payoff requested sooner carries fewer months of penalty and interest.

  • Check the newspaper list in your county after October 15.
  • Keep the mailing address on the tax bill current.
  • Find the parcel number on your latest tax bill before calling any office.

Can you sell before the land is certified or auctioned?

Yes. Once the taxes are paid, a sale at any point before the auction takes the parcel out of the process. Anyone may redeem, so a buyer can pay the redemption amount, and a title company can arrange that payoff from the sale proceeds.

  • Before certification: pay the county collector, and the title company can take the payoff from the sale proceeds.
  • After certification: request a payoff from the Commissioner by parcel number, and watch the 30 day quote window.
  • Close before the cutoff, which is 4:00 p.m. Central the last business day before the sale.

Cash Home Buyers makes as-is offers on Arkansas houses with back taxes. Keep your parcel number and the sale date from your notice at hand, because the cutoff time controls what is possible.

Frequently asked questions

Can the county sell my house for unpaid taxes in Arkansas?

No. Section 26-37-101 bars sales of tax-delinquent land at the county level. The county certifies it to the Commissioner of State Lands, and the state sells it at auction.

When does the state take title?

When the Commissioner receives the county's certification, which must happen by July 1 of the year after the one-year delinquency period. Title vests in the State of Arkansas, in care of the Commissioner.

What is the last moment to redeem?

4:00 p.m. Central on the last business day before the auction. Partial payments are rejected and do not extend the deadline.

Can I bid on my own house at the auction?

No. The Commissioner's rules bar former owners and interested parties from bidding.

Do I get the extra money if the house sells for more than I owe?

Possibly. Excess proceeds go first to the Commissioner's costs, the county's taxes and other government claims, then to the former owner minus up to $500 for administration, but you must file a claim that meets every requirement.
